description: NormalizedIter::new strips trailing spaces via rposition, so the input slice passed to the iterator never ends with a space. However the pending_space logic (lines 545-554) emits a space and then skips forward — if pending_space is true and pos reaches the end of the trimmed slice, it returns None rather than the pending space. This means a string ending with multiple spaces (e.g. 'foo  ') after trimming becomes 'foo' (trailing spaces stripped), which is correct. But consider an input whose trimmed content ends with a run of internal spaces followed by a non-space that was consumed on the previous call. The pending_space branch at line 549 skips all spaces and then checks if pos < len: if the trimmed content happens to end in a space after the last non-space character was already emitted, the emit is skipped. This is correct. However the code has no test for strings that are entirely spaces (' ') — new() sets start==end==0 producing an empty slice, and the iterator should yield nothing. Verify with a test.
title: NormalizedIter emits trailing space for input ending with internal space sequence
